All 24 tests pass. I implemented the eight operations in `list_ops.py` recursively, per the spec's "without using existing functions" constraint — no `len`, `reversed`, `list.append`, or similar built-ins:

- **`append`** — prepends the head of the first list and recurses on its tail; returns the second list once the first is empty.
- **`concat`** — flattens one level by appending each sublist to the result of `concat` on the rest (so nested lists are preserved, as the tests require).
- **`filter`** — keeps the head when the predicate is true, always recursing on the tail.
- **`length`** — counts by recursion, returning 0 on the empty list.
- **`map`** — applies the function to the head and recurses on the tail.
- **`foldl`** — applies the function to `(acc, head)` first, then recurses on the tail, so the accumulator flows left to right.
- **`foldr`** — folds the tail first, then applies the function with the head as the element argument, giving right-to-left ordering (this is what makes the direction-dependent division tests and the `"exercism!"` string test pass).
- **`reverse`** — reverses the tail and appends the head at the end.

`list_ops_test.py` was left untouched and no new files were created.
